service.description: For the framework's post-receive gitECA rule (Git.gitecas.xml): queue the push pipelines of each branch that moved and the tag pipelines of each tag created, at their new commits, as the user who pushed, and keep the schedules of the default branch (GitPipelineSchedule). Nothing when the engine is off here (git-ci enabled; with it empty, no enabled GitRunnerPool) or the commit has no ci.xml and no component.xml. A push to refs/for/[branch] is no branch's: its merge request's event queues its runs. With authorization disabled only, as a rule's actions run: the user and the commits are the event's.

parameter.name: refUpdates
parameter.description: As org.moqui.GitServices.process#GitEca's

parameter.name: runList
parameter.description: Maps: pipelineRunId, runNum, pipelineName, statusId (queued, waiting or error)

service.description: For the service ECA rule on queue#MergeRequestEvent (GitCi.secas.xml): queue the merge-request pipelines of a merge request that was opened, reopened, made ready or whose head moved (synchronize), at its head commit, for its target branch, in the merge request's repository (whose refs/merge-requests/[n]/head holds the head of a fork's and of a pushed one too). A fork's, a pushed-for-review and a detached merge request's run is untrusted; a hidden one's run is hidden with it (and shown with it: set#MergeRequestHidden). opened for a head that has had its run queues none. With authorization disabled only.
Queue the schedule pipelines whose cron came due since they were last checked (the queue_ScheduledPipelineRuns_frequent ServiceJob). One that fails is logged and the others still run.

Start queued job runs, oldest first, up to each pool's maxConcurrent: a container through the pool's host type, with the server's URL and a job token (the start_QueuedJobRuns_frequent ServiceJob; a run is also started soon after it is queued). A job with no pool, an image its pool does not allow or a host that does not start it is an error. Jobs of a pool of registered runners wait for a runner.

End the job runs past their time limit, the ones whose runner is gone (its container lost or exited with no result) and the queued ones no runner took, then remove from each host the containers of this server whose job run is not running (the end_OverdueJobRuns_frequent ServiceJob). Then a deploy step left waiting is started again, and one that began more than git-ci deploy-timeout-seconds ago and never ended fails.

The retention of run data (the expire_PipelineRunData_daily ServiceJob): artifacts, reports and caches past their expireDate that are not kept, the logs of jobs that ended more than git-ci log-retention-days ago, and log chunks an ended job left. gc#ContentBlobs then deletes the blobs.
The runs of a repository the caller may view, newest first.

parameter.name: refName
parameter.description: A full ref (refs/heads/main)

parameter.name: includeHidden
parameter.description: With authorization disabled: the runs of hidden merge requests too

parameter.name: runList
parameter.description: Maps: pipelineRunId, repositoryId, runNum, pipelineName, definitionSource, event, refName, commitId, mergeRequestId, sourceRepositoryId, triggeredByUserId, ownerId, trusted, protectedRef, hidden, approvalState, approvedByUserId, statusId, statusMessage, environmentId, retryOfRunId, createdDate, startedDate, finishedDate, durationSeconds

service.description: A run with its jobs, in the order needs gives.

parameter.name: repositoryId
parameter.description: With runNum, in place of pipelineRunId

parameter.name: includeSuperseded
parameter.description: The attempts a retry replaced too

parameter.name: jobList
parameter.description: Maps: jobRunId, pipelineRunId, jobName, matrixKey, attempt, superseded, needs (List), context, poolName, runnerPoolId, runnerId, image, statusId, statusMessage, exitCode, timeoutMinutes, logBytes, hasLog, minutesUsed, testCount, testFailedCount, commitStatusId, queuedDate, startedDate, finishedDate, durationSeconds

parameter.name: canUpdate
parameter.description: The caller may cancel, retry and approve

service.description: A job run with its steps, its failed tests and its artifacts and reports.

parameter.name: stepList
parameter.description: Maps: stepSeq, stepName, command, statusId, exitCode, firstChunkSeq, startedDate, finishedDate, durationSeconds

parameter.name: failedTestList
parameter.description: Maps: testSeq, suiteName, testName, filePath, lineNumber, message, durationMillis

parameter.name: artifactList
parameter.description: Maps: artifactId, jobRunId, artifactKind (artifact or report), name, path, sizeBytes, sha256, keep, expireDate, createdDate, fileName, location (its ci-artifact:// location)

service.description: A piece of a job's log. While the job runs: the chunks after afterChunkSeq. Once it has ended (finished): the stored log from offset, as text. A page that tails passes back nextChunkSeq and nextOffset each time, so it loses no line when the job ends; with watch the caller is told of new lines on the notification topic GitCiJobLog (message: jobRunId, nextChunkSeq, finished) for a few minutes after each read.

parameter.name: chunkList
parameter.description: Maps: chunkSeq, stepSeq, text

service.description: An artifact (a tar.gz) or a report of a run and a piece of its content, maxBytes from offset, so a download is read in pieces. A cache is not found.

The pipelines a commit defines, as the engine reads them (its ci.xml, else the built-in pipeline of a component repository), so an application need not parse the file. revision is a branch, a tag, a ref or a commit, the default branch when empty. Needs the view right. Each pipeline: pipelineName, events (push, merge-request, tag, schedule, manual, deploy), manual (run#Pipeline runs it), branches, tags, cron, jobNames.

parameter.name: source
parameter.description: file, builtin, none, or invalid (a ci.xml that is not valid, with errorMessage)

service.description: Send an artifact (a tar.gz) or a report of a run as this request's response, streamed from its content blob a window at a time with Range, ETag and If-Range, as ec.web.sendResourceResponse sends a file: for a screen's download transition, with nothing copied to a file. Read as get#RunArtifact is; a cache is not found. inline shows a passive file (an image, a PDF, plain text, JSON) instead of sending it as an attachment; an active one (HTML, SVG, XML, JavaScript) is still an attachment unless inlineActive is set too. Shown inline it is sandboxed (Content-Security-Policy: sandbox, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff).

parameter.name: inlineActive
parameter.description: With inline, show an HTML, SVG, XML or JavaScript file too. A job's output is whatever its commit's scripts wrote, so set this only for a run whose commits the application trusts: it is shown on the application's host (sandboxed, so no script runs, but it can look like one of the application's pages).

service.description: Keep an artifact or a report of a run past its expiry (keep true: a release's, which the daily retention then leaves), or let it expire again (false). It still counts toward the storage caps. Needs the update right on the repository, or authorization disabled; a hidden run's is found as get#RunArtifact finds it. A cache is not found.
Run a pipeline that has the manual event for a branch or a tag, as the caller. Needs the update right on the repository. The application's run check is asked, as for every run.

parameter.name: refName
parameter.description: A branch name or a full ref; the default branch when empty

service.description: A new run of the same pipeline for the same commit and event, as the caller. A run that was untrusted for where its commits came from stays untrusted. Needs the update right.

Cancel a run that has not ended: its waiting and queued jobs are cancelled, its running jobs ended and their containers removed. Needs the update right, or to be the user who asked for the run. A run that has ended is an error.

Run an ended job again in its run, with the run's trust: a new attempt is queued, the jobs skipped for it wait again, and the old attempt is superseded. Needs the update right. A job that still runs is an error.

parameter.name: jobRunId
parameter.description: The new attempt

service.description: Let a run that waits for approval start (an untrusted run, or one the application's run check held). Needs the update right on the repository, or authorization disabled: an application with roles of its own checks them and calls this with authorization disabled. The run stays untrusted: no secrets, no cache writes, an untrusted pool. A run that does not wait is an error.
The runner pools, each with the jobs running and queued in it.

parameter.name: poolList
parameter.description: Maps: runnerPoolId, poolName, description, ownerId, instanceHostId, poolKind, trusted, enabled, maxConcurrent, allowedImages, cpuLimit, memoryMb, diskMb, pidsLimit, maxMinutes, egressRule, serverUrl, hasRegistrationToken, runningCount, queuedCount

service.description: Make or change a runner pool. A new one is named default, of containers, trusted, enabled, one job at a time, and allows no image until allowedImages names some.

parameter.name: poolKind
parameter.description: container or registered

parameter.name: trusted
parameter.description: false: the pool takes untrusted runs, and only those

service.description: Remove a pool that has no running job, with its registered runners.

A new registration token for a pool of registered runners, replacing the one it had: stored hashed, shown once, and good for validDays (git-ci pool-token-days, 7). With revokeRunners the pool's runners are revoked too, as for a token that leaked. An operator's (GIT_CI_ADMIN, or authorization disabled).
Revoke a registered runner (GitRunner.statusId revoked): its token is refused from now on and the job it runs ends as an error. An operator's.
The secrets of a repository (the caller needs the delete right, a maintainer's) or of an owner (authorization disabled), without their values.

parameter.name: secretList
parameter.description: Maps: secretId, name, scope, environmentId, environmentName, createdByUserId, createdDate, lastUsedDate

service.description: Make a secret or change one, of a repository (the delete right, a maintainer's) or of an owner (authorization disabled). The value is encrypted, written here and never read back; left out on a change, it stays, unless the change moves the secret to another scope or environment, which needs a new value. A name taken in the same scope is an error.

parameter.name: scope
parameter.description: protected (the default), tags or environment

service.description: Remove a secret of a repository (the delete right) or of an owner (authorization disabled).
The environments of a repository the caller may view, or of an owner (authorization disabled). The target and clone URLs only to a maintainer (the delete right) or the application.

parameter.name: environmentList
parameter.description: Maps: environmentId, name, targetUrl and cloneUrl (a maintainer's only), dataTypes, requiredPipeline, approvalRequired, approverGroupId, allowedRefs, hasToken (never the token), lastCommitId, lastDeploymentId, lastDeployDate

service.description: Make or change an environment of a repository (the delete right, a maintainer's) or of an owner (authorization disabled). The target's token is encrypted and never read back. Its secrets go only to a run of a protected ref or of a branch allowedRefs names, never to a merge request's, and with approvalRequired only to an approved run. For deployments (docs/interfaces/Pipelines.md "Deployments"): the target instance (https, or http to a loopback IP literal), the token it issued (at least 32 characters: its component-deploy attestation-secret, which signs each attestation and is never sent), the pipeline with the deploy event that must pass, who approves, and the data types the target loads.

parameter.name: targetUrl
parameter.description: The target instance's base URL

parameter.name: token
parameter.description: Written, never read back; left out on a change, it stays

parameter.name: cloneUrl
parameter.description: The URL the target fetches the repository from (https or ssh, with no user or password in it); the repository's public clone URL when empty

parameter.name: requiredPipeline
parameter.description: The pipeline, with the deploy event, that must pass

parameter.name: approverGroupId
parameter.description: The user group whose members approve; a maintainer of the repository (the delete right) when empty

parameter.name: allowedRefs
parameter.description: Branch patterns, separated by spaces, whose runs get the environment's secrets, and which deploy to it, besides protected refs (a deployment of one no branch rule protects waits for an approver)

parameter.name: dataTypes
parameter.description: The data types the target loads of the component's data files, comma separated, signed in each attestation; empty for the target's defaults

service.description: Remove an environment (the delete right on its repository, or authorization disabled); refused while a secret is scoped to it.

Deploy the head of a branch to an environment of the repository, as the caller (the update right): the environment's pipeline (requiredPipeline, which must have the deploy event) is queued for the commit with the deploy event, so the run check decides as for any run; when it passes the deployment waits for decide#GitDeployment if the environment requires approval or no branch rule protects the branch (an approval of the run does not count), then the deploy step posts an attestation of the passed run to the target's Component-Deploy REST. The branch must be protected or named by the environment's allowedRefs; the target deploys the commit only while it is still the branch's head. A repository the caller does not view is not found. The status deploy/[environment] of the commit follows each move.

parameter.name: environment
parameter.description: The environment's name, or environmentId

parameter.name: refName
parameter.description: A branch, or refs/heads/...; the default branch when empty

parameter.name: commitId
parameter.description: When given, it must be the branch's head

parameter.name: statusId
parameter.description: waiting-pipeline, or failed with message (no such pipeline with the deploy event, a run refused by the run check, pipelines off here)

service.description: Approve or refuse a deployment whose pipeline passed and that waits for approval: by a member of the environment's approverGroupId who views the repository, else a maintainer (the delete right), or the application with authorization disabled; never by who asked for it. An approved one deploys.

parameter.name: decision
parameter.description: approve or refuse

service.description: Cancel a deployment whose deploy step has not begun, with its pipeline's run when that has not ended: by the requester, or with the update right.
The deployments of a repository the caller views, newest first, paged in the database; errorText to a maintainer (the delete right) only.

parameter.name: environment
parameter.description: The environment's name

parameter.name: deploymentList
parameter.description: Maps: deploymentId, repositoryId, environmentId, environment, commitId, refName, componentName, statusId (requested, waiting-pipeline, waiting-approval, deploying, deployed, failed, refused, cancelled), pipelineRunId, runNum, requestedByUserId, approvalRequired, approvedByUserId, approvedDate, refusedByUserId, deployResult (the target's answer as JSON), errorText (a maintainer's only: it may hold the target's own words), createdDate, startedDate, finishedDate

parameter.name: deploymentCount
parameter.description: All that match

service.description: One deployment of a repository the caller views; not found otherwise.

parameter.name: deployment
parameter.description: As find#GitDeployments

service.description: The runner time of a repository (the caller views it) or of an owner (authorization disabled) in a month, from the GitRunnerUsage rows written as job runs end, for an application's quota.

parameter.name: periodKey
parameter.description: yyyy-MM (UTC); this month when empty

parameter.name: artifactBytes
parameter.description: The artifacts and reports stored now

parameter.name: cacheBytes
parameter.description: The caches stored now

service.description: Remove every run of a repository with its jobs, steps, logs, artifacts, failures, usage, secrets, environments and schedules, and stop its running jobs: what delete#GitRepository does of itself, for an application that clears a repository's pipelines and keeps the repository. Needs the delete right, or authorization disabled.

What the service the conf names (git-ci run-check-service) implements: asked, with authorization disabled, before a run is queued, so the application can refuse it or hold it (a quota, pipelines turned off), say an untrusted run may start without approval, lower its trust, and name whose secrets and usage it counts under. With no service, or no decision, a trusted run is allowed and an untrusted one waits. An error it leaves refuses the run with that message.

parameter.name: trusted
parameter.description: The engine's answer

parameter.name: decision
parameter.description: allow, wait (for approve#PipelineRun), refuse, or skip: queue nothing and write no run and no status (the repository's pipelines are off). Asked too, with pipelineName ci.xml and jobCount 0, before an error run for a pipeline file that is not valid; skip writes none.

parameter.name: trusted
parameter.description: false lowers the engine's answer; true never raises it

parameter.name: message
parameter.description: Shown on the run and its statuses when it waits or is refused

parameter.name: runnerPoolId
parameter.description: The pool the run's jobs use, in place of the one their pool attribute names; it must still take the run's trust

service.description: What the service the conf names (git-ci run-url-service) implements: the page of a run, for the target of its jobs' commit statuses. With no service, no url from it (a repository whose page is not the application's) or a service that fails, the conf's run-url template is used.
